title: Railway Pricing 2026: Plans, Usage Rates and Costs
summary: Railway pricing combines a monthly plan fee with metered charges for CPU, memory, storage and egress. See which cost drivers affect your bill.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


After you have priced your workload, most of the questions left are about the edges of the bill rather than the rates, and each answer below points back to the pricing and docs pages.


Is Railway free to use in 2026? Yes: Railway has a trial with a small starting credit, and after it ends the account reverts to the Free plan with $1 of credit per month; usage beyond that is billed on metered usage.


Treat the free credit as a way to measure your workload's CPU, memory, storage and egress, then price those meters at the paid rates.


### What happens when my Railway credit runs out?


When the trial ends, your account reverts to the Free plan with $1 of credit per month, so **a forgotten project can still run into the Free plan's limits** .


On a paid plan, usage past what the plan includes is billed at the metered rates instead of being cut off. Which of those you face depends on your plan, so confirm it in your billing settings before relying on a project in production.


### Does Railway charge for an idle service?


Yes, for whatever the service holds. A running service reserves memory and may use little CPU, and storage and volumes are metered whether or not traffic arrives. The practical consequence is that "low traffic" does not mean "near zero bill".


If a service really is intermittent, check Railway's docs for its sleep or scale-to-zero behavior and test it against your usage, because that setting changes which meters keep running.


Egress between your own services is a separate question. Railway documents private networking inside a project, and you should read how it treats internal traffic versus traffic leaving to the public internet.


Price those two paths as different line items, because public egress is the meter that tends to surprise people.


### Can I cap my Railway spending?


Yes. Railway lets you set usage alerts and a spending limit in the dashboard, and the difference between them matters.


An alert tells you a threshold was crossed and the bill keeps growing. A hard limit stops usage, which protects your budget but can take your service offline.


Decide which failure you can tolerate, a surprise invoice or an outage, and set the one that matches.


### How often does Railway change its pricing?


Assume rates and plan terms can move at any time, because Railway doesn't publish a schedule. The pricing page is the only source that reflects what is current.


Keep dated notes of the rates you used, re-run your workload against the page whenever your traffic shifts, and compare the result to your earlier notes before you commit to a bigger deployment.
